q: Who founded Dallas in 1841 at a crossing of the Trinity River?
fact: Bryan, a Tennessee-born trader, built a cabin on the east bank of the Trinity and is credited as the city's founder.

q: Which U.S. Vice President is Dallas most often said to be named after?
fact: He served under James K. Polk. The true origin of the name is still debated, and some say it honors a different Dallas entirely.

q: In 1855, European settlers founded La Réunion near Dallas. What was it?
fact: Largely French, Belgian and Swiss, the colonists were inspired by Charles Fourier. The colony collapsed within a few years, but many settlers stayed and shaped Dallas's culture.

q: In what year did a great fire destroy much of Dallas's downtown square?
fact: The July 1860 blaze probably began when matches ignited in the Texas heat, though panic over rumored abolitionist arson led to harsh reprisals.

q: Which railroad reached Dallas in 1872, followed a year later by the Texas and Pacific, making the city a rail crossroads?
fact: The crossing of two rail lines turned Dallas from a small town into a commercial hub.

q: Dallas grew rich in the late 1800s as a major inland market for which crop?
fact: Dallas became one of the largest inland cotton markets in the world, and its banks and insurance firms grew alongside it.

q: The State Fair of Texas, held at Fair Park, first opened in which year?
fact: It is among the largest annual state fairs in the United States.

q: Which newspaper, founded in 1885, is Dallas's major daily?
fact: It was launched by A.H. Belo and Company, and its publisher George Dealey later gave his name to Dealey Plaza.

q: In what year was the department store Neiman Marcus founded in Dallas?
fact: It was founded by Herbert Marcus, his sister Carrie Marcus Neiman and her husband Al Neiman.

q: The Adolphus Hotel, opened in 1912, was built by a man famous for what product?
fact: Adolphus Busch, the St. Louis brewer, built it, and it is still a downtown landmark.

q: The Dallas neighborhood of Oak Cliff was annexed by Dallas in which year?
fact: Oak Cliff was once its own city, and today it is home to the Bishop Arts District.

q: Highland Park Village, opened in 1931, is notable as one of the first of what in the United States?
fact: Its Spanish Revival design became a model for the modern shopping center.

q: The Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas serves which numbered Federal Reserve District?
fact: Dallas was chosen as one of 12 cities for a Reserve Bank in 1914.

q: Dallas Love Field is named for Moss L. Love, who was what?
options: An Army aviator killed in a 1913 crash
fact: Love Field opened as an Army training airfield in 1917.

q: Which wildcatter's East Texas oil strike in 1930 helped make Dallas an oil-finance center, after H.L. Hunt bought his leases?
fact: Hunt made a fortune from the field and based his empire in Dallas.

q: Fair Park hosted what major event in 1936?
fact: Its Art Deco buildings from that event are the largest collection of 1930s exposition architecture in the U.S.

q: Southern Methodist University opened in which year?
fact: SMU's Dallas Hall was modeled on Thomas Jefferson's Rotunda at the University of Virginia.

q: Dallas Union Station, next to Reunion Tower, opened in which year?
fact: It was built to consolidate the city's several rail lines into one depot.

q: When it was introduced in 1947, which area code was assigned to Dallas?
fact: 214 was one of the original area codes, and 972 and 469 were later added as overlays.

q: The 1892 Dallas County Courthouse, built of red sandstone, is known by what nickname?
fact: It now houses the Old Red Museum of Dallas County History and Culture.

q: The Dallas Zoo, opened in 1888, is the oldest zoo in which state?
fact: It is often called the oldest and largest zoo in Texas.

q: White Rock Lake was created as a reservoir in what year?
fact: It is now a popular recreation spot, and local lore holds that a ghostly Lady of the Lake haunts its shores.

q: The song "Big D" popularized Dallas's nickname. In which musical was it introduced?
fact: Frank Loesser's 1956 musical gave the city its enduring nickname.

q: El Fenix, founded in Dallas in 1918, claims to be the oldest chain of what?
fact: Founded by Miguel Martinez, El Fenix helped popularize Tex-Mex cooking nationwide.

q: 7-Eleven grew out of the Southland Ice Company, which started in what Dallas neighborhood in 1927?
fact: An employee began selling milk, bread and eggs from the ice dock, and the store was renamed 7-Eleven for its original 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. hours.

q: Braniff International Airways, based at Love Field, shocked the airline world in 1965 by doing what?
fact: The "End of the Plain Plane" campaign used designer Alexander Girard and colorful aircraft.

q: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport began operations in which year?
fact: DFW covers about 27 square miles, larger than the island of Manhattan.

q: Who was Dallas's first elected woman mayor, serving from 1987?
fact: Strauss was a popular civic booster whose name is now on a downtown arts square.

q: Who became Dallas's first African American mayor in 1995?
fact: Kirk later served as U.S. Trade Representative under President Obama.

q: When Dallas was founded in 1841, Texas was what?
fact: Texas joined the United States in 1845.

q: On what date was President John F. Kennedy assassinated in Dallas?
fact: He was shot while riding in a motorcade through Dealey Plaza.

q: Dealey Plaza is named after the publisher of which newspaper?
fact: George Bannerman Dealey was a longtime civic leader, and the plaza was dedicated in 1940.

q: Which Dallas museum, opened in 1989, is located on the building's sixth floor where shots were fired?
fact: It occupies the former Texas School Book Depository.

q: Who filmed the assassination in the famous 26-second home movie?
fact: Zapruder was a Dallas dressmaker, and the film is among the most studied in history.

q: Where were President Kennedy and later Lee Harvey Oswald both pronounced dead?
fact: Parkland is a major Dallas public hospital.

q: Who swore in Lyndon B. Johnson aboard Air Force One at Love Field, becoming the first woman to swear in a president?
fact: The ceremony was held in the stifling heat of the grounded plane.

q: Oswald was arrested in which Oak Cliff movie theater?
fact: The theater still stands and now hosts films and events.

q: Where was Oswald shot by Jack Ruby on November 24, 1963?
options: In the basement of Dallas police headquarters
fact: The shooting was carried live on television.

q: What nightclub did Jack Ruby own?
fact: Ruby ran it on Commerce Street.

q: President Kennedy was on his way to a luncheon at which Dallas venue when he was shot?
fact: The Trade Mart was a wholesale showroom center, and the motorcade was headed there when it passed through Dealey Plaza.

q: The John F. Kennedy Memorial in downtown Dallas, a cenotaph, was designed by which architect?
fact: A cenotaph is an empty tomb, and Johnson's open-roofed design was dedicated in 1970.

q: What marks the spots on Elm Street where the shots struck?
fact: Visitors often dart into traffic to take photos of them, which is dangerous.

q: A month before JFK's visit, which U.S. ambassador to the UN was struck by a protester's sign in Dallas?
fact: The October 1963 incident was a sign of the tense political climate in the city.

q: Dealey Plaza was designated what in 1993?
fact: The plaza and surrounding buildings are protected for their role in the assassination.

q: What does the term "cenotaph" mean, as in the JFK Memorial?
fact: The word comes from the Greek for "empty tomb".

q: How tall is Reunion Tower, whose geodesic ball opened in 1978?
fact: The ball houses an observation deck and a revolving restaurant.

q: Bank of America Plaza is the tallest building in Dallas at how many feet?
fact: The skyscraper is outlined in green lights at night.

q: Fountain Place, a glass prism skyscraper downtown, was designed by the firm of which architect?
fact: Pei also designed Dallas City Hall and the Meyerson Symphony Center.

q: The red neon Pegasus sign atop the Magnolia Hotel was the logo of which oil company?
fact: It began as the symbol of the Magnolia Petroleum Company and has been a Dallas icon since 1934.

q: Dallas City Hall, opened in 1978, features a dramatic what?
fact: I. M. Pei designed the building, which looks like a leaning wall and appears in the movie RoboCop.

q: The Meyerson Symphony Center, opened in 1989, is home to which orchestra?
fact: It was designed by I. M. Pei and is known for its acoustics.

q: The Dallas Arts District is billed as the largest contiguous what in the United States?
fact: It spans 19 blocks and hosts the Dallas Museum of Art, the Nasher, the Winspear Opera House and more.

q: The Nasher Sculpture Center, opened in 2003, was designed by which architect?
fact: Piano also designed the Kimbell Art Museum's addition across the Metroplex in Fort Worth.

q: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science, opened in 2012, was designed by which architect?
fact: Its cube shape appears to float above the ground.

q: Which Spanish architect designed the Margaret Hunt Hill Bridge over the Trinity River?
fact: The bridge's giant white arch is a signature of the Dallas skyline.

q: Klyde Warren Park, opened in 2012, was built over what?
fact: It is a deck park over Woodall Rodgers Freeway connecting downtown and Uptown.

q: Thanks-Giving Square's chapel, designed by Philip Johnson, has a spiral stained-glass window called what?
fact: The window by French artist Gabriel Loire spirals upward toward the sun.

q: Pioneer Plaza in downtown Dallas features how many bronze longhorn steers?
fact: The steers and three trail hands recall the cattle drives that passed through Texas in the 1800s.

q: General admission to the Dallas Museum of Art has been what since 2013?
fact: The museum dropped its general admission fee and launched a free membership program.

q: The Kalita Humphreys Theater in Dallas is the only freestanding theater designed by which architect?
fact: It opened in 1959 and is home to Dallas Theater Center.

q: How tall is the modern Big Tex, the State Fair's cowboy mascot?
fact: The original Big Tex was a Santa Claus built in Kerens, Texas, and the State Fair of Texas bought him around 1951.

q: In what year did Big Tex burn in an electrical fire at the State Fair?
fact: A new Big Tex was unveiled in 2013.

q: What fried treat was introduced at the State Fair of Texas in 1942?
fact: Fletcher's Corny Dogs are still sold at the fair.

q: The Texas Star at Fair Park is a famed what?
fact: At 212 feet it was billed as the tallest Ferris wheel in North America.

q: The Dallas Arboretum is on the shore of which lake?
fact: The garden covers about 66 acres.

q: Deep Ellum gets its name from a pronunciation of which street?
fact: Locals shortened "Deep Elm" to "Deep Ellum".

q: The Bishop Arts District, known for shops and restaurants, is in what Dallas area?
fact: The district is named for Bishop Avenue, and its restored storefronts are now a hub for local shops and restaurants.

q: The Wyly Theatre in the Dallas Arts District is known for being what kind of theater?
fact: Its stage tower can be rearranged in many configurations.

q: Dallas's "Mixmaster" refers to what?
fact: It sits where several highways come together near downtown.

q: Which wholesale center, opened in the late 1950s, is billed as one of the largest of its kind in the world?
fact: The Dallas Trade Mart was developed by Trammell Crow.

q: The SMU Meadows Museum is known for having one of the largest collections of what outside Spain?
fact: It was founded by oilman Algur H. Meadows.

q: In what year was the red neon Pegasus first installed atop the Magnolia Building?
fact: It was lit up as part of the Magnolia Petroleum Company's advertising.

q: The Majestic Theatre, opened in 1921 in downtown Dallas, originally hosted what kind of shows?
fact: It was part of the Interstate Amusement circuit.

q: The Hall of State at Fair Park, built for the 1936 Centennial, celebrates what?
fact: Its murals and statues honor figures from the state's past.

q: The Cotton Bowl stadium at Fair Park was built in which year?
fact: It was originally called Fair Park Stadium.

q: Which sculptor's "Dallas Piece" stands outside Dallas City Hall?
fact: The abstract bronze was installed in 1978.

q: The Winspear Opera House was designed by the firm of which British architect?
fact: It is home to the Dallas Opera and the Texas Ballet Theater.

q: Who was the first head coach of the Dallas Cowboys?
fact: Landry coached the team for 29 seasons, from 1960 through 1988.

q: What was the Cowboys' record in their first season in 1960?
fact: They became a perennial contender within a few years.

q: The Cowboys got the nickname "America's Team" in which year?
fact: It came from an NFL Films highlight reel that year.

q: The term "Hail Mary" for a desperate pass was popularized by Roger Staubach's 1975 playoff throw to whom?
fact: Staubach said he closed his eyes and said a Hail Mary.

q: Which Cowboy holds the NFL career rushing record with 18,355 yards?
fact: Smith broke the record in 2002.

q: How many Super Bowls have the Cowboys won?
fact: They won Super Bowls VI, XII, XXVII, XXVIII and XXX.

q: The Cowboys' 1990s dynasty was powered by "The Triplets," Troy Aikman, Emmitt Smith and which receiver?
fact: The trio led Dallas to three titles in four years.

q: Jerry Jones bought the Cowboys in 1989 for about how much?
fact: He then replaced Landry with Jimmy Johnson.

q: Texas Stadium, the Cowboys' old home, was famous for having what in its roof?
fact: Texas Stadium opened in 1971 in Irving.

q: AT&T Stadium, the Cowboys' current home, opened in 2009 in which city?
fact: It is often nicknamed "Jerry World".

q: The Cowboys' practice facility and headquarters, The Star, is in which city?
fact: It opened in 2016 and includes a hotel and an indoor stadium.

q: The original Dallas Texans of the AFL, owned by Lamar Hunt, later became which team?
fact: They moved to Missouri in 1963.

q: Lamar Hunt coined the name "Super Bowl" after seeing his kids play with what toy?
fact: He suggested it jokingly, and it stuck.

q: The Dallas Tornado won which championship in 1971?
fact: They were one of the league's early powerhouses.

q: The Dallas Mavericks entered the NBA in which year?
fact: Their name came from the TV western Maverick.

q: Mark Cuban bought the Mavericks in 2000 for about how much?
fact: He became one of the NBA's most visible owners.

q: In 2011 the Mavericks won the NBA championship over which team?
fact: Dirk Nowitzki was the Finals MVP.

q: Dirk Nowitzki was born in which country?
fact: He spent his entire 21-year career with Dallas.

q: The American Airlines Center, home of the Mavericks and Stars, opened in which year?
fact: It is located in Victory Park.

q: The Dallas Stars moved to Dallas in 1993 from which city?
fact: They had been the Minnesota North Stars.

q: The Stars won their only Stanley Cup in 1999 against which team?
fact: The series ended in controversy over a disputed skate in the crease.

q: Which Stars great scored the most goals ever by a U.S.-born NHL player?
fact: His statue stands outside American Airlines Center.

q: The Texas Rangers, who play in Arlington, were formerly which team?
fact: They moved to Texas in 1972.

q: The Rangers won their first World Series in 2023 against which team?
fact: It was a dramatic run through the playoffs.

q: The Red River Rivalry between Texas and Oklahoma is played each year at which Dallas site?
options: The Cotton Bowl at Fair Park
fact: The stadium is split down the middle between burnt orange and crimson fans.

q: In 1987 SMU football received what unprecedented NCAA penalty?
fact: The program was shut down for the season for recruiting violations.

q: Which SMU running back won the 1948 Heisman Trophy?
fact: The Doak Walker Award for top running backs is named for him.

q: The SMU "Pony Express" backfield of the early 1980s featured Eric Dickerson and which other runner?
fact: Both later played in the NFL.

q: Which golfer grew up in Dallas and won the 1968 and 1971 U.S. Opens?
fact: Trevino was known for his humor and his unorthodox swing.

q: Jordan Spieth, a Dallas native, won which major in 2015?
fact: He also won the U.S. Open that year.

q: Dallas native Michael Johnson became the first man to win which Olympic double in 1996?
fact: He ran a then-world-record 19.32 in the 200 meters.

q: Byron Nelson set the PGA Tour record of how many consecutive victories in 1945?
fact: He won 18 times that year, and Dallas's tour stop bears his name.

q: FC Dallas began play in 1996 under what original name?
fact: The team was renamed in 2005.

q: The Cowboys' defense of the late 1960s and 1970s was nicknamed what?
fact: Bob Lilly and Randy White were among its stars.

q: Reunion Arena, former home of the Mavericks and Stars, was demolished in which year?
fact: It opened in 1980.

q: The Cotton Bowl Classic moved from Dallas to which stadium in 2010?
fact: It had been played at the Cotton Bowl since 1937.

q: The Cotton Bowl hosted matches during which international tournament in 1994?
fact: It was the only Texas stadium used.

q: The Cowboys won Super Bowl XXVII over which team?
fact: Dallas won 52-17.

q: Which Naval Academy Heisman winner quarterbacked the Cowboys to two Super Bowl wins in the 1970s?
fact: Nicknamed "Captain America," he served in Vietnam before his NFL career.

q: Tony Dorsett set an NFL record with a run of how many yards in 1983?
fact: It was against the Vikings, and it is the longest possible run, which can only be tied, never broken.

q: In what year was Texas Stadium imploded?
fact: The Cowboys had moved to their new stadium in Arlington the year before.

q: The WNBA's Dallas Wings moved to Arlington in 2016 from which city?
fact: They had been the Tulsa Shock.

q: The Mavericks lost the 2006 NBA Finals to the same team they beat in 2011. Which one?
fact: Dwyane Wade starred for Miami in 2006.

q: In February 2025, the Mavericks traded Luka Doncic to which team?
fact: The trade stunned fans, and Anthony Davis went to Dallas in the deal.

q: In which round of the 2016 NFL Draft did the Cowboys select Dak Prescott?
fact: He took over when Tony Romo was injured.

q: What was the signature accessory of Tom Landry on the sidelines?
fact: He rarely showed much emotion, and the hat became part of his image.

q: The Cowboys won Super Bowl XXX in 1996 over which team?
fact: Larry Brown, a Cowboys cornerback, was the game's MVP.

q: Who was the first player drafted in Cowboys history, in 1961?
fact: He became the team's first Hall of Famer.

q: The Texas Rangers' Globe Life Field, with a retractable roof, opened in which year?
fact: It replaced Globe Life Park next door in Arlington.

q: In 2024, the Mavericks reached the NBA Finals and lost to which team?
fact: It was Dallas's first Finals trip since 2011.

q: Dallas restaurateur Mariano Martinez invented what in 1971?
fact: He adapted a soft-serve ice cream machine, and the original is in the Smithsonian.

q: Chili's was founded on Greenville Avenue in Dallas in which year?
fact: It started as a small burger joint.

q: Sonny Bryan's Smokehouse, a Dallas barbecue institution, opened in which year?
fact: The original Inwood Road location was a tiny shack.

q: Half Price Books, founded in Dallas in 1972, started in what kind of place?
fact: Its founders sold used books to pay the rent.

q: Frito-Lay is headquartered in which Dallas suburb?
fact: It is a PepsiCo company.

q: Dave & Buster's opened its first location in which year?
fact: The Dallas Market Center site combined dining, games and drinks.

q: Mary Kay Cosmetics, founded in Dallas in 1963, is known for rewarding top sellers with what?
fact: The first pink Cadillac was given in 1969.

q: Dr Pepper, a Texas favorite, was invented in which Texas city in 1885?
fact: It was created at the Old Corner Drug Store by pharmacist Charles Alderton.

q: The Big Tex Choice Awards at the State Fair honor what?
fact: Winners have included fried butter and fried cookie dough.

q: Which blues legend performed in Deep Ellum and recorded for Paramount in the 1920s?
fact: He is known as the "Father of Texas Blues".

q: Which folk-blues singer, famed for "Goodnight, Irene," played Deep Ellum with Blind Lemon Jefferson?
fact: He later became a prominent folk singer in New York.

q: Robert Johnson's final recording sessions took place in Dallas in what year?
fact: They were held at 508 Park Avenue.

q: Which pioneer of the electric blues grew up in Dallas and once led Blind Lemon Jefferson around the streets?
fact: His song "Stormy Monday" became a standard.

q: Guitarist Stevie Ray Vaughan was born in which Dallas neighborhood?
fact: He was born in 1954.

q: Which neo-soul singer born in Dallas attended Booker T. Washington High School for the Performing and Visual Arts?
fact: Norah Jones attended the same school.

q: Meat Loaf, who sang "Bat Out of Hell," was born in which city?
fact: His birth name was Marvin Lee Aday.

q: Which band, fronted by Edie Brickell, released the 1988 hit "What I Am"?
fact: They formed in Dallas.

q: Rapper Vanilla Ice, who had a hit with "Ice Ice Baby," was born in which city?
fact: It was the first hip hop single to top the Billboard Hot 100.

q: The choral rock band The Polyphonic Spree formed in which city in 2000?
fact: They typically perform in white robes.

q: Which actress and singer was born in Grand Prairie, Texas?
fact: She is from the Dallas area.

q: Which actor was born in Dallas in 1968?
fact: He grew up in Dallas with his brothers Luke and Andrew.

q: The TV series Dallas, about the Ewing oil family, premiered in which year?
fact: It ran until 1991.

q: In the 1980 cliffhanger, who shot J.R. Ewing?
fact: The episode revealing the shooter drew about 83 million viewers.

q: Southfork Ranch, where the TV show Dallas was filmed, is in which town?
fact: It is near Dallas and now a tourist attraction.

q: Which actor played J.R. Ewing in Dallas?
fact: He was also the star of I Dream of Jeannie.

q: The film Dallas Buyers Club won Matthew McConaughey which Oscar?
fact: It is set in Dallas in the 1980s.

q: Which sci-fi film used Dallas City Hall as the headquarters of OCP?
fact: Though the film is set in Detroit, it was shot in Dallas.

q: Which TV action series starring Chuck Norris was filmed in the Dallas area?
fact: It ran from 1993 to 2001.

q: The 1976 film Logan's Run used which Dallas site as its futuristic city?
fact: Dallas's modernist architecture fit the sci-fi setting.

q: Which metal band formed in Arlington in 1981?
fact: Dimebag Darrell was one of its founders.

q: Which country trio formed in Dallas in 1989?
fact: They were formerly the Dixie Chicks.

q: Which outlaw couple met in West Dallas in 1930?
fact: Their crime spree ended in an ambush in Louisiana in 1934.

q: Norah Jones, who attended a Dallas arts high school, was raised in which Dallas suburb?
fact: She was born in New York but grew up in Texas.

q: Dallas Theater Center, founded in 1959, performs at which Frank Lloyd Wright-designed theater?
fact: It was founded by Paul Baker.

q: Which Oscar-winning actor was born in Terrell, east of Dallas?
fact: He won Best Actor for Ray.

q: Which alt-country band led by Rhett Miller formed in Dallas in 1993?
fact: They are known for their energetic live shows.

q: Jack Kilby invented the integrated circuit at which Dallas company in 1958?
fact: He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2000 for it.

q: Kilby's first integrated circuit was built on which material?
fact: Silicon became the standard later.

q: Texas Instruments introduced the first commercial silicon transistor in which year?
fact: It was developed by Gordon Teal.

q: Texas Instruments began as a seismic exploration company called what?
fact: It was renamed Texas Instruments in 1951.

q: Which TI toy debuted in 1978 and appeared in E.T.?
fact: It used a speech synthesis chip.

q: Ross Perot founded which Dallas data-processing company in 1962?
fact: He sold it to General Motors in 1984.

q: Ross Perot received about what share of the vote in the 1992 presidential election?
fact: It was the best showing for an independent in decades.

q: Which company moved its headquarters to Dallas in 2008?
fact: The telecom giant came from San Antonio.

q: Which bank moved its headquarters from Detroit to Dallas in 2007?
fact: The move was meant to reflect its growing Texas base.

q: Which game studio in Mesquite, near Dallas, released Doom in 1993?
fact: The studio helped define the first-person shooter.

q: Which game studio, founded in Dallas in 1996 by John Romero and Tom Hall, made Daikatana?
fact: It was known for ambitious ideas and a famously troubled launch.

q: Which Garland-based studio released Duke Nukem 3D in 1996?
fact: It was formerly known as Apogee.

q: Which video game retailer is headquartered in Grapevine?
fact: It runs thousands of stores worldwide.

q: Kenneth Cooper, the "father of aerobics," founded his clinic in which city?
fact: His 1968 book Aerobics inspired a fitness boom.

q: UT Southwestern Medical Center's Brown and Goldstein shared a 1985 Nobel Prize for work on what?
fact: UT Southwestern has had several Nobel laureates.

q: Southwest Airlines was founded by Herb Kelleher and which cofounder?
fact: Its first flights began in 1971.

q: The Wright Amendment, which limited flights from Love Field, was passed in which year?
fact: It was fully repealed in 2014.

q: DART, Dallas's light rail, is the longest light rail system in what?
fact: It covers about 93 miles.

q: Dallas Love Field's airport code is what?
fact: DFW belongs to the larger airport.

q: Which Irving-based company makes Kleenex tissues?
fact: Irving is a Dallas suburb that is home to several large corporations.

q: Dallas is the ninth-largest city in the U.S. by population in which 2020 count?
fact: The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex is much larger.

q: The Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex is which-largest metro area in the U.S.?
fact: It has more than 8 million people.

q: DFW Airport covers about 27 square miles, making it larger than which place?
fact: It is one of the largest airports in the U.S.

q: In 2011, DFW hit 100 degrees or more on how many days?
fact: It was an extreme drought summer.

q: In October 2019, a damaging tornado struck which part of Dallas?
fact: It was rated EF3 and left a long damage path.

q: Which river runs through Dallas?
fact: The Elm Fork and West Fork join near downtown.

q: I-635 in Dallas is also known as what?
fact: It is named for Lyndon B. Johnson.

q: Dallas hosted which political convention in 1984?
fact: Ronald Reagan was renominated.

q: The George W. Bush Presidential Center is located on which campus?
fact: It opened in 2013.

q: Highland Park, an enclave inside Dallas, was incorporated in which year?
fact: It is one of the wealthiest areas in Texas.

q: The McKinney Avenue Trolley, or M-Line, is notable for being what?
fact: It runs vintage-style trolleys through Uptown.

q: The Great Trinity Forest in Dallas is the largest urban what in the U.S.?
fact: It covers thousands of acres along the river.

q: Dallas is the county seat of which county?
fact: The county was created in 1846.

q: Which Texas city is Dallas's neighbor to the west?
fact: The two cities form the metroplex.

q: What nickname is often used for the DFW area?
fact: The term combines metropolis and complex.

q: In which time zone is Dallas located?
fact: It observes daylight saving time like the rest of Texas.

q: What is the all-time record high temperature at DFW Airport?
fact: It was reached in June 1980 during a brutal heat wave.
